body: The Madu River (looks more like a lake) and its numerous small islands are a protected reserve under the Ramsar Convention (According to Wikipedia, the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands. It is also known as the Convention on Wetlands. It is named after the city of Ramsar in Iran, where the Convention was signed in 1971). The water is greenish and not clear. About 100 boats provide visitors with a ride through mangroves and visiting some islands. A demonstration of cinnamon peeling is seen on the eponymous Cinnamon Island where one can purchase quality cinnamon and related products. There are restauarants by the banks where one can have a good meal. Stalls built on stilts are also seen in the river which sell king coconut and other thirst quenchers.
title: A novel experience

body: The Madu river cruise was the highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka. Our guide Luba, from Luba tours collected us from our hotel at 7:30 am on Saturday 7 October 2017. He explained that in order to miss the crowds, it was advisable to do the cruise early in the morning. Our tour was pre-booked and paid for as part of a 4 day tour, so I’m not sure exactly how much it costs and there was no boards advertising prices. On arrival we were given a bottle of water and a life jacket that we had to wear. We were fortunate that our boat had a canopy and when it started to rain our guide put up the canopy so that we did not get wet. The canopy was lowered when we passed under low lying bridges. At this stage we also had to bend our heads as the bridges were quite low. Our boat had a local guide and our guide Luba. Luba did an excellent job of pointing out the various bird species as well as the various monkeys and reptiles. We stopped at Cinnamon Island, where one of the local men explained how cinnamon sticks and powder is obtained from cinnamon bark. We were also give a complementary cup of cinnamon tea. We were able to purchase cinnamon oil and some cinnamon sticks to take home. Throughout the cruise, the scenery was breath-taking. Luba pointed out the fresh water prawn farms and we were also able to watch the local men fishing. We requested Luba to stop at a floating shop so that we could purchase coconuts. The vendor cut open the coconuts and we were able to drink the coconut water using a straw. It was really refreshing and cost Rs 100 per coconut. A young boy with a monkey approached our boat and for Rs 100, he allowed my sister to hold and take photos with the monkey. We gave the fish farm a miss. Since we had an early start, our cruise was very peaceful as we were the only boat on the water for a long time. The cruise lasted 1 ½ hours and we thoroughly enjoyed the trip. We would definitely recommend it to our family and friends.
title: Amaizing Madu River cruise

body: One the way from Galle to Colombo our driver suggested to take one hour safari at Madu river to see the mangrove threes, animals and it suppose to be really nice. He mentioned a price between 1500 LKR (10USD) to 2000 LKR. Not thinking much I said yes. When we arrived at the place our driver's "buddy" already waited and he charged us 4500 (for 3 people, so 1500/per person). The boat was very old (super smelly after the engine started) and had perhaps 6 sets in total. The tour was in total one hour along the river (surrounded by mangrove threes), we drove by some temples, islands and stop at the place/island where they showed us how cinnamon is made. For a few small cinnamon stick they charged us 400 LKR. Later at the grocery store we bought cinnamon sticks 3 times the amount for 250 LKR!! The boat ride was nothing spectacular, we saw perhaps 2 birds, few monkeys and a cloudy river as river. And as mentioned from other reviews there were tons of tourists. Thinking back for 3h safari (+1.5h drive from and back the hotel) we were charged 6500 LKR and now for 1h boat ride we were charged 4500 LKR. Unfortunately I was not thinking/calculating at the time and as it was quite a spontaneous decision I also did check other reviews on Tripadvisor. I did not expect from our driver to suggest us this rip-off after being with us for 11 days. I did confront him about the situation and he basically said why did I not negotiate. At the end I subtracted the tip from the driver accordingly. Not sure how the entire system works there - if they are multiple providers or not for the river boat safari. But I just want to warn people to be very careful not to heavily overcharged by the river safari.
title: Suggested by our driver - a complete rip off!

body: Our boat ride for visiting various areas of the Mangroves was smooth. Avoid the Cinnamon Island. I think best time for visit will be early morning.
title: Interesting Place

body: We took a river trip through the mangroves and while we thoroughly enjoyed it we were shocked how crowded it was and how pricey it was. It’s such a beautiful location but there was a strong smell of diesel due to too many boats. We were disappointed to see one of the attractions was a baby monkey being shown off in a canoe. Poor wee thing should have been enjoying life in the wild. We did enjoy the visit to Cinnamon Island. That was interesting. Another time I would choose a quieter location. Maybe the Bentota River.
title: Very commercialised.

body: We went on a trip with Jayantha tours and were satisfied about the price and the quality. Tour took a little over 1,5 hours and we saw the temple, went to cinnamonisland, drove through the mangroves. We skipped the fishfarm. Guide hardly spoke any english. He showed us some animals. It was nice to be on the water with temperatures around 30 degrees Celsius. It is a nice trip but if you don’t do it, there is no need to feel sad.
title: Nice trip

body: very enjoyable and varied safari. Visited the cinnamon island and saw monkeys and an amazing temple.
title: River boat safari

body: Madu River safari is a must do ride.. Would suggest an early morning or evening ride ... The guides helped us spot a number of birds, snakes , water alligators.. was a bit scary and adventurous..The fish SPA was fun.. took a lot of conviction to dip my feet first... but after a minute got used to the fish nibbling at my feet... The cinnamon tea and demo at the cinnamon island was memorable.... Had the best king coconut on the safari from a shop on the river...
title: Serene & picturesque

body: 20 $ per person is not worth it, its a commission place. not to be visited, place is ok ok, but too expensive. for foreign tourist its worse. its a trap this place, better avoid and enjoy bentota beaches
title: HIGHLY EXPENSIVE

body: We went to the Madhu river ride during our stay in Bentota. It costed us 6000 Lankan Rupee, but was worth the money. The Journey was for 45 mins to and hour which ended with a fish Spa.
title: Worth the time

body: There are a number of cruise options.There are around 60 islands of various sizes in the river which turns into more like a lake.You see crab and prawn catching "nets", plenty of birds, water monitors, mangroves and a cinnamon farm.Great way to spend some time.
title: Wonderful unspoilt part of Sri Lanka

body: Having read very diverse reviews, I expect the quality of tours vary substantially. Ours was good: the trip took in a significant range of interesting stops from cinnamon islands to temple islands. My only caution is that the order could be improved and next time I would clarify with the guide: e.g. the foot spa was lovely and would have worked much better after traipsing around the temple barefoot! A slightly different schedule may also have proved more relaxing - the child is well-used to being dragged about but had envisaged the boat trip as an opportunity to take things at a slower pace. We resorted to bribing him after the 4th stop in a short space of time - always a good technique...The Madu is genuinely interesting with regard to stops you can visit and I am glad we went. It's worth noting however that it is less fecund with wildlife than the Bentota - we only saw a couple of water monitors, a monkey and various birds. So depending on your interest, that may also be a worthwhile trip (we saw loads there!)
title: Worthwhile

body: Our guide recommended this tour, sold it as a good place to see lots of birds....basically we didn't ... the obligatory Cormorant was about it. Tried to get us to stop & get off at a 'spice island', fish foot massage and stall/shop that sold coconut water and coke. We declined these offers which were just a way to get foreign tourists to part with their money. We weren't asked if we wanted to stop ... it was just assumed we did. Area pretty...people just after your dosh.

body: We took a tour of Madu Ganga early morning. The tour took about 1.5 hours. The boatman stopped at a number of islands for some activities. Cinnamon island was nice, but the person was keen to sell something to us in the end. The kids were surprised to see floating shops and enjoyed King Coconut water. The highlight of this activity was Fish spa, which was something new for us. While visiting, do bargain to get a better price.

body: Good boat ride at sunset There is fish spar And a shop in the middle of the riverWorth the visitingAlso the cinnamon Island, wouldn't recommend purchasing any cinnamon as it is not really good kind , better purchase from a much more larger storeExperience of seeing how it's done is grate

body: This river safari is recommended.Cost is not displayed anywhere,so,better bargain heavily,without sacrificing the duration,the number of islands you will visit etc.For fish massage,you have to shell out a small extra amount .In cinammon island do not buy anything.All are available at one fourth of the cost in the city supermarkets.Overall if you go with family and friends,this place is worth visiting and you will enjoy.At the beginning before you sit in the boat,you will be given free water bottles and at the end of the trip,you will be given cold drink.Recommended to visit
title: Worth it

body: While staying at the nearby Shinagawara beach hotel we took the opportunity to do a boat trip on the huge Madu river.Got to see a lot of wild life and learn a bit about the many islands in the river system.A recommended tour lasting around 1 1/2 hours.

It halts at Cinnamon island where removal of bark is demonstrated and you are told about its benefits to your health but prices are exorbitant and Indians need not buy from there. Same is the case with Tilapia fish foot massage. We liked the ride and fauna that we got to see like iguana and some birds.Our ride was pre-paid but there are no prices displayed there and every one was being charged different rates. Despite inquiring, seeing that we had the voucher, they did not tell us the price er person.

body: We took a river cruise trip and really enjoyed it. Excellent guide and a trip we are very glad we made.The stops at Cinnamon Island and Temple Island were really interesting and our guide took plenty of time to explain the meanings behind the parts of the temple and the symbolism. We chose to leave a donation for the upkeep of the temple but no requirement to. We came away with a little booklet on Buddhist lessons and history which is aimed perfectly at all ages so great for school RS lessons!We loved the history of the very clever use of every part of the cinnamon plant whether it was fertiliser, making roofs from the leaves as well as cooking the spice itself. The children learned lots in a very short space of time so it was ideal for our 10 and 12 year old.Plenty of things to see in the mangrove swamps and beautiful river. The children particularly loved the King Coconut and fish spa - all included in the price of the trip.Highly recommend for all ages and particularly those with children.

body: A lovely river with many islands with lots of history to same. Fish spa is a must visit place and if you are into angling .. you'd be surprised with what the river has to offer

body: There are many operators running river safaris on the Madu river. The pricing is very tricky and we got a huge discount after some bargaining. Initial price quoted for a boat (for two of us) was LKR 6000 and finally we paid LKR 2500.The ride lasts about 1.5 hours and is fun. You are taken through mangroves and if you are lucky you could spot a water monitor lizard (we saw one up close) and also few bird species. There was a local man on a boat who has a baby monkey (purple face leaf monkey) and you can hold the monkey and take pics. He takes about LKR 200.You will be taken to a fish farm where you can dip your feet among the fish for a wierd feeling foot spa. They give you some fish food and dropping this near your feet attracts a lot of the fish. It is a wierd but fun experience. They charged us LKR200 per head. I saw others being charged more - so again i guess it depends on your bargaining skills.One of the stops will be at a floating shop where you can buy refreshments and finally you will be taken to what they call 'Cinnamon Island'. Here an old man will show you how he prepares cinnamon from the tree branch. He will then offer to sell you some forms of cinnamon - powder, oil etc. We ended up buying the powder and oil for LKR500. Overall it was a fun experience and in my opinion its worth going for the safari

body: Little boat trip Fish foot funny Temple visit no interest they just want money.Mangrooves are Nice.

Gladly will do it again.

body: This one-hour tour takes you on a boat safari through the primitive depths of the mangrove marshes in Madu River. Traverse the dark and dangerous caverns formed by the thick mangrove forests; interspersed with bright open stretches of water. Get a chance to see crocodiles, water snakes, tree snakes and wild boars in their natural habitat. Watch the cormorants; storks and many other avianlife hunt for their prey in swift flow of Madu River. View the pots for catching prawn and shrimp left in some of the shallower areas of the river

body: The voice of the boat very annoying , because the boat old , No I would recommend visitors to attend because you will enjoy nature never

body: Did Madu River Safari with Aitken Spence Travels stunning scenery driving through the mangroves we was lucky to see a couple of water monitors and different birds.We also visited Cinnamon Island which was good

body: Whilst staying at Ceysands Hotel, my husband and I decided to do the Madhu or Madu river (Ganga) safari trip and it was just brilliant! It is a MUST-DO for any nature lover, with a rich ecology system full of mangroves, birds, trees and animals and reptiles. The Madhu river is a huge wetland protected by wildlife convention because of its biodiversity. We went with 'Santa' who has the tour shop on the right hand side of the road as you come out of the hotel gates. His prices are on a billboard so you don't need to get exploited by all the other rip-off tuk tuk drivers that harass you. We still haggled the price down a little (as you do in Sri Lanka). We paid Rs.3700 for both of us in total for the whole trip which included the tuk tuk ride to and from the river, the river boat safari and tour guide and a tuk tuk ride to a gem mine. The whole day was fantastic and a very worth while day trip that lasted about 5 1/2 hrs in total. You can also choose to visit the turtle hatchery too if you wish. In fact, Santa will customise your trip to suit you, but make sure with any trip you do in Sri Lanka, that you confirm prices first! The tuk tuk ride to the Madhu river took about 40 minutes, a lovely way to see the tropical surroundings of Sri Lanka. The river safari was about 3 hrs. The Madhu river had about 64 islands in it but many of the smaller ones have now submerged. There are now just over 20 larger islands and only about 15 of these are large enough to have habitants. The most famous of the islands are the larger Kothduwa Island which is named after it's Buddhist temple and Cinnamon Island. The river safari starts near Balapitiya where it meets the sea, and you head up towards the islands across a mass of water and lake where you will see a whole range of wildlife, there are over 100 different birds and cormorants, kingfishers, herons were everywhere and we saw eagles. There are many reptiles and crocodiles living in this river but we didn't see any crocodiles, just Monitor lizards and chameleons. The people living on this river make their living from fishing (and you will see areas across the lake netted off for their fish farms), and from cinnamon and coconuts...in fact it is famous for the Cinnamon Island where we stopped and watched a demonstration of how the cinnamon was peeled and dried, and enjoyed a complimentary glass of cinnamon tea. Then a demonstration of how the coconut husks were made into ropes, and baskets etc....a very interesting time spent! You can choose to buy (at very good prices) cinnamon oil and cinnamon sticks, powder. The other island we visited was the larger Kothduwa Temple Island. This is famous for its Buddhist Temple so remember to take a sarong or sari to wear to cover legs or shoulders if you want to go inside and if you can't bear the hot floor whilst barefoot, then take socks to wear too. It is a very important Temple as it was once known to have held the relic of the tooth of Buddha which is now in Kandy. There are a lovely long line of Buddha statues lining up which are still being built. There is a school near by and you can see just how happy and tranquil the way of life is here. The river also boasts a wide variety of trees and mangroves which the boat driver may take you in. We also saw monkeys and butterflies. It was a wonderful trip. After we went by tuk tuk to a gem mine where you can see how they operate, and if you wish, you can by gemstone jewellery at the shop. Yes, this is a tourist attraction but from what I saw in town shops, their prices were a lot cheaper...REMEMBER TO HAGGLE! I bought a little pair of sapphire earrings (with a certificate) for just £12 which was 40% off the original price, just show interest but start walking out if its too much...they will shout a better price which gives you something to bargain with. This was one of my husband's best day trips whilst in Bentota, definitely would do it all again!
title: A MUST FOR NATURE LOVERS!

body: Took a boat ride along the madu river. Unfortunately got caught in some downpour but overall the experience was pleasant. We saw a monitor lizard swimming alongside us, visited the feet clensing fish pool.
title: Interesting boat ride

body: If you are visiting Bentota you must try Madu river boat safari. Its a slow boat ride for 1.5 hours which will takes you through different places, temple, Island, Fish spa. we booked through Nilwala River Safari & after bargaining we got the boat for 2000LKR for 3 people which is the cheapest compared to others who offer the same safari. We paid additional for fish spa that again is your personal choice to do it or not. But its worth doing it just cost 200LKR per person & its amazing experience. We visited temple but v read reviews that they will ask for money, the monk was calling us but we didn't go inside otherwise he would have asked for unnecessary tips. Going through Mangroves was fun & different experience.
title: Great Experience

body: We took the trip through Captain Boat House where they charge Rs.2500 per person(Sri Lankan rupee). The boat ride is for one and half hours and takes one through the mangrove caves(just two of them) and one can see several islands along the route. There are 64 islands in total but most of them are uninhabited. we visited the Cinnamon island where we were shown how the Cinnamon is derived from the bark, dried and processed. You will have to tip the person as they provided us with cinnamon tea and for explaining how cinnamon is produced.The ride takes us through two low bridges where we really had to bend our heads low and duck for cover. The green foliage on either side of the river was astounding and the best part was the passage through the mangrove cave.we were lucky to see a Monitor lizard on the shore during our ride. They also showed how the fishermen catch prawns and crab . they have provided trapping mechanism for these with net.All in all an interesting trip
title: Good trip through Mangroves

body: Excellent experience, a must for family while in Sri Lanka..gives insight to certain aspects of life and development in the Area. The guides were very polite and showed the entire Area. AN experience in itself. my daughter and wife enjoyed the trip
title: Made River Safari

body: The river safari is absolutely great. There are few hotels which you can go. It's cheaper. Go to fish therapy for sure. It's great. It's cheaper if you go to a hotel and use their package. There is a Buddhist temple in there as well. Better to go there. Cinnamon island also there. Good place to go!!
title: Very good and amazing experience

body: Relaxing. See new things. Interesting to have this tour. In general it was good and I'll do it again
title: Good ride

body: A sanctuary rich in biodiversity. One of the world's primary mangrove conservations. The river safari is full of actions and an experience not to be missed.
title: A river safari not to be missed

body: It was an excellent experience for my 2 friends from India and my family. They were planning to do a boat safari at Bentota River but I recommended and brought them to do the “Madu River Safari”Our boat provider was “Totupola Maduwa River Safari No.2” and must specially mentioned about the boat driver ‘Nishantha, he was excellent. The fear Rs.3000/= was very reasonable and the time spend was really worth for the money. The boat ride was for about 2 hrs. They are located 50-75 M after the bridge on the western side of the main road towards Galle next to the “Bord’ eau” restaurant.If you are keen in seeing the crocks and the birds must start early around 6-7 am, the ‘Fish foot massages’ an attraction you must not miss on the way.
title: "Excellent day out with friends and family"

body: From the moment I stepped into the boat, I felt like all my emotions has changed. You will become another person. The Cinnamon island is fantastic, they shows you how they make the cinnamon. The Buddhist temple is such a mystic in a lovely location.Highly recommended to explore whenever you are in Sri Lanka!
title: Romantic

body: The river safari is rather fun. There is a cave , fish spa and cinnamon island to visit. I went with 20 family members and it costed us 3500 for the boat ride, 200 pp for the fish spa and 200 for the cinnamon packets at the island. The rates are higher for non nationals I gather. A quick tip- ask the boat rider to put the roof above the boat, we discovered the roof rather late so we ended up with headaches. The safari is a must do and takes about 1.5hours in all
title: Amazing experience

body: The excitement reaches the peak when you pass through the mangroves which looks like doing a jungle safari on boat. The fish spa is great to experience. The visit to cinnamon island adds spice to the whole trip.P.S. The cost of hiring the boat is negotiable
title: Exciting jungle boat safari

body: We saw a few blue jellyfish in the saltwater river, and also a few birds. However you need an expert with you to show you the sights and where the wildlife live.
title: Biodiversity not far from the main road

body: For me this was the most relaxing and serene moment of the entire Sri Lanka tour. We took a boat trip down the river/lake and enjoyed every minute of it. The price was 3000 rupees per adult, half price for children. We asked for fishing equipment and were provided two rods and some bread for bait and we managed to purchase some shrimp as more serious bait from the guy "operating" the fish foot spa. We mostly caught catfish that we released but it was very nice nevertheless. We loved gliding on the river, among and along the mangroves, we saw plenty of beautiful birds (awesome blue kingfishers, majestic eagles), some iguanas and very big squirrels on the trees, and giant jellyfish in the water. We visited the Cinnamon island to see how cinnamon is made and visited the Buddhist temple on the island in the middle of the lake where we even got some blessing threads from the monk. Passed under a lot of very low bridges (had to "bow down" to pass under them. The last one had the train track on it and we went under right when the train went over, so we literally went under the train and survived!! The kids were over the moon!! Very very charming afternoon surrounded by amazing nature. The boats have sun canopies which is nice to protect you from the sun. Bring water and some snacks.
title: Super relaxing dive in nature

body: As you settle down in the boat, you are soon taken into a mangrove forest, epic as it sounds, it actually is.One by one you are taken to several interesting stops. Fish Spa, Cinnamon Tea, Buddha temple are some of them. Your 'captain' also shows you some jellyfishes or kingfishers in the middle of the water. You will also learn how prawns are caught from the river water. I am sure you wont miss it if you plan to visit Lanka !
title: Mangroves, Fish Spa, Cinnamon Tea & Buddha temple on this Boat Ride !!

body: It has something entertaining for all age groups. This is a 75-90 mins boat drive covering around 21 small islands ( read as patch of islands ). Has a amazing mangrove forests and one can actually see different species of these mangroves forests. there were many sightings of monitor lizards and monkeys in these forests. Seeing these lizards cruising through the waters is fun to watch. After the boat ride starts one can visit various islands ( optional ), its got a temple, cinnamon garden, many fish spa huts. It was a excellent 90 mins spent on this safari. Choose off summer season as hotter days tend to spoil your day, plan well and enjoy the nature,
title: great outdoor activity with nice boat ride

body: Once you get over the initial tickles, it was very refreshing and interesting. Try to choose the tank with the small fish. They are less ticklish.
title: Very nice!

body: Boat ride in the Madu river was a great experience on a sunny day. The ride among the mangrove and the fish therapy was very good.
title: Boat safari.

body: We went on a ride with Captains Deck.The boat tour was for 2 hours including Fish Spa.It was a great ride covered around the islands , they gave the option to go to some islands .Friendly guide.There was a goid restaurant next to river bank with quality food at reasonble rate.
title: Great boat ride

body: Went on a 3 hour boat trip (2500rs). Stopping at fish massage, cinnamon island and other. A must when in the region...
title: Boat trip

body: This is one of the many rivers which falls in to the Indian Ocean from Southern Sri Lanka. It has over 100 little islands spread over. Boating through the mangroves was a beautiful experience.
title: A peaceful boat ride

body: We enjoy a lot in our madu ricer safari. As we went there around 3.30 pm the safari was not much sunny and tired. It is one of safe river journeys in Sri Lanka which any one could enjoy with there little toddlers. I went there with my 1 year old baby.With in the boat safari the boat rider will take you to some commercial islands including cinnamon island and also temples as well. also we saw 5 cent island and prawns squares which grows prawns,Overall Madu river safari is not an awesome trip but a nice place to visit and my opinion about the safari is worth watching place.

body: WE had booked a river cruise through our hotel and it was kind of disappointing. We saw one monkey and a crocodile which was so far away, was hard to see. Went through a small mangrove but that was about it. They try to get you off the boat to go visit Cinnamon Island, fish therapy and a Temple (we did the Temple) but it is just a way for them to get more money.. All in all disappointing and wouldn't rush to recommend it

body: We've been recommended by our driver on this boat safari. The entrance fees they ask for at the first place was the double of market price. The tour guide barely speaks English, we are supposed to have a 2 hour safari experience in the mangrove but finally spent 1 hour, haven't seen anything interesting! Waste of money and waste of time!!!!
title: Horrible experience

body: Great little trip organised for us by Suranga tours , located on the beach from Riu Sri Lanka, short drive from our hotel, the four of us on a boat that seated nine, nice ride up the river lined with mangroves, saw monkeys, had a fish pedicure , stopped off to see how cinnamon is produced, any wildlife was pointed out , saw how they fished for prawns.. excellent trip
title: Lovely ride up the Madu

body: We went with a driver from the hotel and we were the only ones on the boat so we could pick and choose where we stopped. We saw eagles, monkeys and enjoyed a relaxing river cruise. we visited a temple on one of the islands which was inspiring and informative. They will always ask for donations.
title: Peaceful and relaxing visit

body: A very sound and calm place with ancient temple and people while fishing. you can visit with friends and family and enjoy the Fish therapy as well.
title: Madu River and Boat Ride

body: We visited the goverment sponsored eco-education centre on the east side of the lake, where we learned about the mangroves and wildlife, had a local cooking demonstration ending up with a delicious home-cooked dhall curry, cinnamon cutting demos too. Later we tried fishing on a raft in the lake, caught some small catfish which we threw back, and then went on the boat tour. Loads of bird life to view, saw meter long monitor lizards too but no crocs. Oh and got very wet as it poured with rain when we were halfway round the lake on the other side of the island. Oh well - it's fairly warm rain.
title: Loads of wildlife

body: Nice to take a boat along the Madu River. There are lots of boat operators in the area to accommodate visitors. The area has some nice mangroves along the banks of the river and lake, but not exceptional. If you're lucky, you will see monkeys and various bird species. Pleasant outing.
title: Lined with mangroves!

body: The best way to see the Madu Ganga Biodiversity Area is by boat and there are lots of boat operators in the area to accommodate you. Costs vary depending on the number in your group. The area has some nice mangroves along the banks of the river and lake, but not exceptional. If you're lucky, you will see monkeys and various bird species.
title: Boat thru Ramsar site!

body: The first 20 minutes of the cruise, frankly, was quite unbearable. The din of the noisy engine which reeked of gasoline/diesel at the slow start of the course was rather unpleasant.We coursed through some dense mangrove tunnels which I would consider to be the highlight of the cruise, and also passed by some prawn farm traps. Along the way, the boatman would point out cormorants, Sri Lankan kingfisher, iguana as he spotted them.We made 3 stops: - a brief stop at a hut where a short demo on how the cinnamon bark was stripped and dried to produce the cinnamon sticks which we used in our cooking. We made the obligatory purchase of a few packets of sticks, powder and oil each for 100 LKR. - a stop at a very old Buddhist temple- a stop at new 'attraction' for foot massage by fish The whole cruise of 1.5hrs cost usd25.
title: Noisy sputtering boat engine marred cruise through the Madu

body: This is my 2nd time to visit and i used same agent Madu Queen Boat Safari, ya..the owner name is Sujeewa.I was came from dehiwala train station to ambalangoda, we purchase 2nd class ticket, cost lkr 130 per person, my journey start at 7.20am to 8.55am.They arranged tuk tuk to pick us up, because my last visit was 2 years ago 😁😁, i paid lkr 300.They start with briefing of visit area and entering the boat. This time i didnt used life jacket (dont follow me ya..)Madu river has 65 small islands, 1 big island which is cover 2 schools, tampel, hospital and market; the small island no one can live there because it is very very small 😬My trip was cover: seeing black bird, fish treatment (fish treatment you need to pay lkr 200, they will gave you fish food) this is still thw most important thing to do 😙, cinnamon island, tampel island and lagoon. This boat safari took 3.50 hours.We are end up at the owner house for lunch, they provide lunch beside the river.Boat safari cost lkr 4,000 per boat, lunch cost it is reasonable and taste good for our asian tongue.My advise, you should applied sunblock otherwise you will really burn just like me; wear hat..Enjoyyy 😙😙
title: Still the best place to escape from my routine

body: Madhu River is a big River. It seems like a big lake. We have to drive almost 40 km from Bentoda to reach here for boating in River. We hired a boat and have a nice fun about 2 hours. There are so many isle land. We visited 3 isle land. We have paid 7000 Sri Lankan rupees for a separate boat with machine. A memorable boat ride.
title: A THRILLING EXPERIENCE

body: We went to the river safari hoping to see some wildlife but we didn't see any. Even though the" captian" said we may see many just so that we will pay for the rides . It's USD 20 per adult but u can pay in rupees which is better cos of the exchange rate. The boat ride itself is about an hour on a rickety open boat with plastic chairs . But it's an interesting experience for the kids . Only plant life usually spotted . The boat man tried to take us to cinnamon island and fish spa. But u can decline
title: Interesting experience but expensive

body: The best place in Sri Lanka where you can find a big diversity of mangrove trees and fauna living in a wet land.
title: A RAMSAR Wet land.

body: This place is protected under RAMSAR Wet land conservation.Many varieties of mangrove trees can be seen here including a huge bio diversity. You can have a boat ride through mangrove trees and a fish therapy for your feet. There are so many little islands in this river.
title: RAMSAR Wet land

body: Actually we saw only one monkey and it belongs to somebody, but cute anyhow. Our boat driver was the coolest one on that day driving his boat more fasten than the others. We also visited in a fish farm, where the fishes "eats" our foot.... Also the cinnamon bay was a nice place to visit. Though it was a tourist place, don't miss this one.
title: Mangrove trees and monkeys

body: Keep your expectations low and this will be an awesome experience. Not many wildlife to see but the trip was still memorable. We passed through low-height bridges (had to get down in the boat or bang!), through mangroves, to a Buddhist temple, a Hindu temple in the middle of lake.Also visited and saw how cinnamon is prepared. The best thing was fish spa. You can get these in cities but in lake is a totally different thing.I would have given 5 stars if they hadn't denied sharing a boat with different group/couples so we had to take a boat all for ourselves. 6000 Srilankan Rupees. 1.5 hr trip.
title: Amazing boat experience

body: Wonderful experience. Two hours worth every second.See the traditional Shrimp farming techniques used by the locals,Learn the ways of local Cinnamon Farmers,Take a turn in floating fish spas,Learn about the local community at the Temple Island, "Koth Doova"And most importantly, Have a relaxing break into the nature.
title: Voyage through wilderness

body: fish spa and the boat ride in hidden mangroves is one of the best feelings ever had!!! A must feel!There are enough and more places that provide boat rides. The famous one is Captain;s boat house but we found out that to be a bit expensive... If you put a walk along the area you can find some competitive rates and good places.. one such we found was Green mangrove or Green mango place.
title: Superb experience

body: We had visited to Madu river in our last leg of our Sri Lankan tour but it was the best way to conclude our Sri Lankan tour. The back waters is very beautiful. You can sight variety of birds and also monkey are there for you entertainment. One can also visit fish therapy centre feed the fishes and get a pedicure. There is also a small place where your demonstrated how cinnamon is extracted and one can also buy variety of cinnamon based products. All together nice place but pls carry sunscreen lotion along with you and also don't forget to use ur sunglasses. Excellent place to spend time.
title: Good place to visit....

body: Perhaps we expected something similar to the backwaters of Kerala and our expectations were a little too high but we found our boat trip around Madu River to be just ok (maybe a 3.5 stars). It's pleasant enough to travel up and down a part of the river but, apart from a few birds (they certainly were not abundant), we didn't see any wildlife. The only people we met was on a couple of islands - one selling cinnamon spice, the other looking for donations for a small religious temple. In total, the trip lasted about an hour and twenty minutes.
title: Pleasant enough but nothing special

body: Very good trip visited spice island temple there is also a fish farm saw monkeys and birds went trough the mangrove tunnel a a very enjoyable trip
title: very good

body: Maybe I just expect a lot and get disappointed. I would say its very average. The only awesome part is the 5 to 10 mins of going thru a mangrove. body: Wonderful riverboat cruise down the river , abundant bird life, cinnamon spice demonstrations, visits to an ancient temple etc etc
title: Lazing down the river

body: The calm waters, the mangrove bushes, the shrimp fishers, the fish treatment places and the big Maduganga lake itself was a memorable experience. The munk at the Kotdoowa Rajamaha Viharaya temple demanded a donation in exchange of a short prayer and a piece of thread tied round your wrist!
title: Nice sceneries

body: Expect the usual mangrove ride, nothing exotic. Greenery is eye pleasing, water a little smelly. Good for relaxation
title: The usual

body: Awesome experience, i recommend going for the special safari which is just Rs 1000 more, where they take u through the mangroves. We went in madu queen safari.

body: Reasonably priced River safari. You get a complimentory fish foot massage. Boats go through Mangroves which is a good experience. You can by cinnamon at an Island. Good quality cinnamon for 400/- Srilankan rupees.

body: Went to Madu River on an office trip. It was a nice experience though I didn't enjoy the boat ride in the sun. Still, the area is vast and getting closer to the mangroves was worth it. body: The Madu river in Balapitiya is very picturesque with 64 islands which houses many animals and birds. Many tour operators offer boat safari. The mangrove caves, cinnamon island, snake island and link at the sea are beautiful.
title: Excellent location

body: Madu ganga is situated in Balapitiya, along the country's southern coast , within the Galle District of the southern Province of Sri Lanka. The Best River safari In Srilanka. Me And My Friends have lot of fun.
title: Boat Safari In Madu River Best

body: This was pretty amazing. You board a tinny...very safe and head off through the mangrove tunnels and out into the quite vast wetland . You can stop at various islands on the tour around this large lake are.. Cinnamon island being one where you can purchase some cinnamon, drink tea or have a massage. Prawn nets and fisherman and cormorants and bird life flash past. Excellent trip.
title: Boat safari Spectacular

body: So peaceful!! So amazing!!! The temple in the middle is unbelievably moving!! I would recommend anyone to visit!!
title: Amazing

body: A one and a half hour boat tour around wetlands. An archipel where there used to be 64 islands. Today 25 islands still remain. Some are inhabited. We made stops at a cinnamon plantage, a buddhist temple and a fish farm. Nice to see but all asked for money so make sure you bring some cash. The trip itself costed us 6500LKR for two persons. We had a private tour. Our guide was very knowledgable about the wildlife and history of the islands. Pleasant time on the water but very touristy..
title: A boat trip

body: Just finished an hours Boat trip in the Madu River which flows around an Archipelago of 64 islands. We started from a base close to where the River flows into the Indian Ocean. Verdant foliage, birds, water monitors and even a crocodile sighted. Gayan piloted the boat and was very knowledgeable about these Wetlands.The Madu River supports an extensive eco system.I had never heard of this place before and my thanks to my driver cum guide who knew of these excursions and joined me for the boat ride.
title: An Excellent 60 minutes cruising the Madu River

body: Lovely relaxing boat trip lasting 1.5 hours. The cost was 5000 rupees for 2 people. The river is huge with lots of wildlife to be seen. The boat stops at 2 islands, first the cinnamon island where you can watch how cinnamon is extracted, with the opportunity to purchase some cinnamon products, the second island is the Buddhist temple. We also had the opportunity to drive the boat which was fun. Overall a great experience, would highly recommend.
title: Enjoyable trip

body: An hour and a half cruise down the Madu river...with stops at a fish farm where u dip your feet in and get tickled by fish...they go bananas when the guy throws in pellets and it turns into a tickling frenzy.In addition, they also stop by an aptly named cinnamon island...where an old man shows you how they harvest cinnamon and explains the Madicinal properties of cinnamon powder, oil and stem. You could also buy some from the old man at a reasonable price.Later there's a short break at a floating snack bar and on the way back u may even run in to a young boy with a ' purple face ' monkey on a canoe. Of course for a small fee u can take pictures with the cute little critter.My kids enjoyed it and by the looks of it so did a lot of other families we saw on the river.If you are lucky, you may even get to see a crocodile in its natural habitat.
title: Nice experience

body: It was a good solid 1.5 hours of boat ride with a few pitstops in between.The Cinnamon island is good and the live demo is nice. The waters are very calm and its a pretty good sight to watch the birds around.
title: Awesome Visit !!

body: This is a wonderful attraction which I fully recommend. Our guide was humorous and informative, a shame I didn't note his name. Go early to avoid the crowds. Very relaxing and beautiful scenery.
title: We loved our boat ride and fish foot therapy.

body: A very soothing boat ride through the mangrove caves and on the lake. The stop at cinnamon island was fascinating, and we bought some cinnamon goodies for reasonables prices. The fish therapy is quite overstated, but nevertheless a nice experience. Worth the price. The manager is a very friendly person and lives up to the standards of a captain in the boat house!
title: Great experience

body: Lovely ever cruise among beautiful mangrove forests, can dip your feet into fish ponds for fish therapy, float through tunnels of mangroves, birds, wildlife and Cinnamon forests with experience of how they make Cinnamon. Carry a hat or cap as it can be sunny hot. Loads of fun.
title: Super experience with diverse activity !

body: We were 11 of us in total, 6 adults and 5 kids and we had one boat. We all fit in the boat. Cost us US$75 for an 1 hour boat ride. It was raining but the cover kept us somewhat protected. It's a lovely river boat ride - hardly any animals, or information from the tour guide and you have to duck when you go under the bridges. Kids loved it.
title: Fun experience without a tour guide

body: Madu Ganga ( River) is a unique lagoon setup in Balapitiya ; South West Sri Lanka. Boat safari in the lagoon is a good excursion for few hours. It was so disappointed that we were not provided any demonstrator. I would recommend to tour with someone who got thorough knowledge about this setup as you cannot just read a book and understand this unique set of environment. Fish Spa is available in riverside and I felt so sad about the stressful fishes who were moving in a small room. Because of the large number of boats rides have badly affected the fishes and trees in the lagoon. Overall the experience is great and it could have been better with a professional knowledge.

body: This is a great place to visit while tourng the down south of Sri Lanka. It looks pretty ordinary from the boat house surroundings but when you start the boat tour you realize what a wonderful palace is this. Do not forget to visit the temple in the lonely island which dates back to many centuries.

body: Didn't see many mangrove inhabitants as expected and at best a few kingfishers and eagles. One of the islets we were brought to had a live demonstration of how cinnamon oil was produced. Nothing much else to see. Took the cruise enroute to Galle. Time would have been better spent at Galle instead.

body: A boat ride in Maadu ganga is a better way to spend a weekend with family or friends if you love the nature.The boat ride will take 2hrs to 2hr30 along the river visiting isles and seeing mangroves.majors attractions on the river are isle where cinnamon production is done & Kothduwa Raja maha Viharaya (A buddhist Temple) and fish foot massage.No entrance for the temple or cinnamon isle but for fish foot massage will cost an additional amount.
title: Best way for a family or friends outing

body: Madu ganga is rich with different mangroves and isles.you would come across with some birds or vertebrates too.A better way to relax and feel the nature..
title: Feel the nature

body: We went to Madu river expecting to see many animals. You pay a 20USD boat fee and you go river ip making different stops. We were told we could see crocodiles but we didn't see any and once in the boat they tell you that crocodiles are rarely seen. There are very few animals, we could see only a couple of birds and a water monkey. Also you do different stops to see how the cinnamon is collected, a buddhist temple, some people on boats with monkeys they let you catch for a tip, fish massage factories... Nothing amazing. The main issue is that after having paid 20UD you are being asked money by everybody on any stop you make and also the boat driver is asking you a tip. As a tourist you should be very careful as any individual will be there only with the objective of "extracting" you money. We left that place with a very sad impression...
title: Overrated, few animals to see, expensive and everybody trying to get money from you

body: We had 'ticked' the boat ride in Madu River without expecting much - we had seen the waterways in Kerala - so what can be different ?But the ride in the river turned out to be very nice. We regretted that we had not set aside the time to visit the islets where people (called cinnamon islands) - people who live in the islets extract cinnamon in the traditional way. We also did not have time for fish massage !But then the boat ride itself was nice - as it weaved to dense mangrove area. We also saw the traditional way of fish nets being laid - quite different from hat we have seen elsewhere. The highlight was the setting sun ! We did not stay behind to see the sun actually set on the horizon, but even then the sight was brilliant.I would recommend visitors to set aside at least 4 hours which will give enough time to visit the islets, get foot massage done, and maybe even have refreshments in the small floating eating place.
title: Vegetation and Islets in the River make it interesting !

body: What an amazing boat ride!It took us about 2 hours to ride down the river; the captain of the boat (who was also our guide) stopped at all of the islands and made sure to describe each. Also, anytime that he noticed any birds or animals he approached as close as possible to give us look. Cinnamon island was very cool. The temple was beautiful. The fish foot massage was indescribable! That was the best part of the trip ... dangling your feet into a pool of fish!Totally recommend this trip. It was the highlight of our vacation.

body: We visited the river as part of the trip. There are many islands to check out but the most impressive was the cinnamon island and the lovely man who lives there showed us how he makes cinnamon and oil, he explained how to use the oil and was just super nice. I particularly liked the mangroves and the Buddha temple on the river.

body: Fish massage is very good and it's very cheap. Just you have to pay Rs. 200 LKR for the fish massage

body: I should imagine most hotel visitors to Ahungalla have no idea what is just up the road. We took an early morning, 7am boat so we were first on the river. 22 islands on a river/lake community. Cinnamon island very educational. Saw so many kingfishers and huge water monitor lizards. Loved it

body: An experience you will truly enjoy. The fish attraction is a ripoff. The cinnamon production area is interesting.

body: It is a 1 & 1/2 hours boat ride (Rs. 2000/2500 for locals) around the river. You will be able to see so many tiny islands covered with mangrove. There are arches made by mangrove too. Then the most important thing is "Fish therapy", Rs.200 per person for locals.And also you could visit the cinnamon island and get an idea about making cinnamon sticks. body: This trip is great fun! Lovely and relaxing trip with plenty to visit. There was loads to do! Just worth a visit on a morning. Great to see the mangroves as well. Very friendly staff also!

body: We did this as part of our organised day trip so everything was sorted out in advance for us. We had a boat just for the 4 of us and our guide, our first encounter was with a young lad in a canoe with a baby monkey who came and put it in our laps! He obviously expected a tip so we gave him some rupees then carried on to the fish pedicure. This was fantastic fun and I really recommend it - there were about 6 pools of fish of differing sizes from the very tiny to some around 8 inches long. If you're hesitant about trying it don't be - just do it! We also visited an island where they grow cinnamon and one with a Buddhist temple. Oh and a young lad brought a baby mongoose over as well. All in all it was a really great trip and an enjoyable couple of hours.
title: Great value for money - take a guide with you though

body: There was very good scenery on this but the river is much travelled and it felt a little tired with the guide that we had. There was an expectation of a tip when nothing additional had been done. The cost is minimal making the trip ok.
title: The tour was provided with good service

body: Great little stop and ride on the water. It is kind of touristy but we enjoyed getting out of the car and we are boat people so we enjoyed a ride around...
title: Nice break from the car

body: Friday morning, 9 am, the 7th October and we picked up our prearranged tuk tuk, just down the road from our hotel, Riu Sri Lanka, the driver was taking us to the Madu River for our river safari.Our journey time was less than 15 minutes and we were taken to one of the places offering river safaris. The one we were taken to was no doubt a friend of the tuk tuk driver as we were not charged a fare. We agreed a price for the trip, with the owner, which was 4,000 Rupees (approximately £20) this was for both of us, we thought this was good value, certainly when compared with some charges mentioned in other TripAdvisor reviews.Apart from the boat driver and our guide, the Tuk Tuk driver we were the only 2 people on the boat. We were strapped in to our life jackets and the adventure began. The first thing we encountered was a young lad in a canoe with a monkey, who charged for a photo.The boat weaved in between the mangroves in search of the wildlife and scenery. We saw several eagles, water monitors, small crocodile, monkeys and some other unidentified birds.Also as part of the trip we visited Cinnamon Island where we saw the process of producing the cinnamon spice. Some old guy gave a demonstration of the production of cinnamon, once the demonstration was complete the spice in all its forms was proffered up for sale.We also visited another island, where there was a Buddhist Temple, Kotdoowa Rajmaha Viharayo (reviewed separately), well worth stopping here.The river is littered with loads of little islands. There are a number of shops in the river, bits of wood on stilts, these offer coconuts for sale. Some of them offer foot massage, you put your feet in the water and little fish nibble away at them, we decided to give this a missOk we did not see a vast number of animals as we had anticipated but we really did enjoy our trip, good value and would recommend it.As the UK Tour Operators wouldd not be coming to Sri Lanka till 7th November, there were no organised tours, we arranged this ourselves, with some assistance from a member of staff from the hotel. We did not use the people on the beach. Our trip lasted 2 hours.
title: Enjoyable river trip

body: Interesting trip. Enjoyed seeing the wildlife, visiting a Buddhist temple and Cinnamon island. gave us a taste of the area.
title: Interesting river trip.

body: A boat ride in river madu is a nice way to end your busy day. You will be able to experience fish massage as well during your boat ride visits. Although the rate is high, visit to all the islands will worth it. There are bridges across at some places and you will need to bow your head. But the view is quite nice and small floating shops would be quite a sight!

body: We really enjoyed having this half-day excursion in Hikkaduwa. It offers a nice break from the beach and is very easy going, you'll see crocodile, temples, cinnamon stick making in this ride through the branches of the river. It is not cheap depending on the size of the boat and how many people are going (and all the stops are obviously in order to make you buy something) but it is definitely worth doing.
title: A great boat excursion

body: The visit included learning about cinnamon and other local trades. We had fun on the water and learned about local trades.
title: Fun Visit

body: Amazing river safari with Captain Joe who had lots of good things to say and showed us many things on the mighty Madu. A dashing good looking captain that obviously had good training and could handle the boat well. We will say the high seas with him any day. Some of the other companies that operate were driving far too fast and their boat drivers looked like they had never sen a boat before. Captain Joe was calm at the helm and kept us safe and in control - Well done Captain Joe!

body: Quite relaxing 3 hours tours with beautiful views and amazing mangroves around, they had 2 stops on island, 1st at the cinnamon island which was not quite interesting, they were more interested in selling some oils and soap. other stop was at a temple and fish spa which was quite good. weather was quite good it rained 2 times on our trip. Quite reasonable around 50 usd for a private boat. A must do experience on trip to Srilanka.

body: The trip was wonderful , very nice things to see. Tour guide/boat driver was very informative. But, upon arrival we were asked to pay $100 for the boat rent ( we were 2 adults and 2 children ages 3 and 5) i found it expensive comparing to other touristic places. I bargained him down to $70 .
title: Very nice scenery bit expensive

body: Excellent well worth a couple of hours away from the beeches Nice to see all types of marine life and also loads of land animals
title: Mr

body: very expensive attraction. spend about 90 minutes on water / boat. enroute attractions are optional and as you add them it costs more. cinnamon groves live demos and sales are informative.

body: It is a very large areas of river that can be visited. Best is Cinnamon Island. Where you can see how Cinnamon made. A small demonstration is given. You can buy the products, such as original spice, powder, soap, oil etc. They are expensive but you should go for it as they are original produce of kind.Next we were treated to Spa Fish for for LKR 200 you can stay as long as you want. body: We were charged USD50/- for the 1.5 hr boat ride on the river. While the river is huge, i think the one in Brunei is better with more wildlife. I also find this place a bit too commercialised with fish spa, cinnamon garden, etc. Maybe its individual opinion i would love to enjoy more of the wildlife along the river than having the boatman constantly asking if you want to do this or do that.... body: We had time spare on our trip so our guide suggested we do this. We had 3 teenage kids with us and even they loved it. We paid 7,000 rps for the boat. Started off where we met a guy on a canoe who rescued baby monkeys so we had a baby monkey join us, that was a highlight. Tip paid.Then moved on to the island with the temple. met a monk who blessed us and asked for a donation, cheeky sod! Then went to the cinnamon island, had a demonstration and bought some spices. Then went to the fish farm and had our feet nibbled, 200rp per person.Trip took about 1 1/2 - 2 hours, we loved it, Overall between tips cost over 10,000 rp but it was huge entertainment value for us, kept 3 teenage kids amused and that is some going.Oh very rare but did I mention that we got chased by an angry cobra while out of the river. Even our skipper had never seen that. They kill easily we got away quick...
title: Loved it..snakes, monkeys, monks, nibbling fish and cinnamon...

body: This is a very relaxing way to spend a few hours on this big river exploring the many islands. body: We arrived just before sunset and our driver/guide arranged for a private boat tour of this wonderful wetland mangrove ecosystem! We paid 4000LKR for the two of us and tipped our guide nicely as he spoke English very well and was very informative/friendly. Coming from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, we have something similar with the Everglades however this was much more impressive and so glad we decided to take this tour. Such a variety of birds, fish, and animals to see. It was declared a RAMSR World Heritage Virgin Wetland in 2003.
title: A wonderful sunset boat tour of this pristine mangrove forest!

body: We travelled to this area as part of an organised day out to the nearby city of Galle. On arrival we were met by the very friendly staff and a very welcome refreshing cold drink. We then set out with our guide ( sadly I don't have his name) on the river cruise that lasted approximately 2 hours in a small boat which was equipped with life jackets and a collapsible roof which came in very handy in the heat of the mid morning sun.During this trip we visited 3 separate islands and saw many sights en route. Our guide would frequently stop the boat to show us the local wildlife which included Monkeys and Eagles. He even stopped to pick some fresh Cashew Fruit and nuts which he prepared for us on the boat. We went through the Mangrove Caves which were fantastic for photo opportunities.The first island we stopped at was the fish therapy where you could have hundreds of tiny fish massage your feet for 200 rupees per person (approx £1) We then travelled to Cinnamon Island were we where able to see the cinnamon being harvested and the process of turning it into sticks, powder or oil. You will be ask to buy something but a small bottle of cinnamon oil only costs 500 rupees (£2.50) and it is well worth it for the experience alone.Last stop was to the Buddhist Monastery, again the guide took the time to explain the meaning behind many of the buildings and beliefs. Before leaving we were taking to see one of the monks who gave us a tradition Buddhist blessing. This island is completely free to visit but you can make a donation if you like. There is no set amount and no pressure. Just time for a lovely slow leisurely sail back to the base again with time to stop for photos of local wildlife and even a quick stop to make a 'flower necklace' for my partner. All in all this was a fantastic few hours and I would throughly recommend it to anyone.
title: Fantastic day out

body: Our boat cruise on Madu River Wetland (Madu Ganga Ramsar Wetland) was not in the itinerary but our driver / guide pulled in on route from Galle to Columbo. It was called Captains Safari. The facilities at the base were rather tired looking although there was a good collection of historical photos to look at whilst we waited.Not at any stage did I see a written price list which seems to confirm the suggestions of previous reviewers that it's all about getting as much as they can.We paid 8400 Rupees for a private boat with just my wife and I. Some boats were more like a bus with up to 16 people.The boat had a canopy which could be raised when the sun was especially hot and was lowered when we had to pass low bridges or when going through mangrove tunnels.We went under low bridges, past prawn traps, went through 3 mangrove tunnels and visited Kotdoowa Rajamaha Viharaya Temple, Cinnamon Island & a fish farm.At Cinnamon Island, we witnessed how cinnamon bark was removed from the stem and dried. Then came the sales pitch. A tray comes out with various cinnamon products - powder, oil, soap, candles. Unfortunately for them, our guide had already stopped at a 'spice farm' on the outward leg of our 2 week tour, and although not specific to cinnamon, we had the opportunity to buy spices there.We also saw coconut leaves were weaved into a roofing sheet, but again, we had seen this earlier in the tour.At the fish farm we saw tourists shouting with delight at red tilapia fish nibbling at their toes.During the trip, we saw a monitor lizard, fish Eagles and a kingfisher.Theses animals were interesting but not that special as I am sure that the noise (and pollution) from the boats frightened a lot of the more interesting animals away.The whole boat trip took 1½ hours, but I suspect longer trips are available.In summary, I think if you live in a city this trip is quite interesting, but it does seem to be about asking for tips at every opportunity.
title: Reasonable, but tired facilities

body: Madu River is located in Balapitiya. It took us almost 90 minutes’ drive from our hotel Citrus to reach the place. Our driver/guide took us to Captains boat house who arranged for the boat ride in the river. After paying 20$ per head towards boat ride we boarded a motor boat with canopy for a ride in the river. Though it appeared a bit costly the ride did justify the amount paid.There are many islands in the river but we visited only two of them mainly cinnamon islands and an island where an ancient Buddhist temple is located. During the ride you can see many places which are stop over places for fishing. The ride is really exciting going through mangroves and crossing low bridges where one has to bend down to avoid getting hurt by hitting the bridges. The canopy of the boat is also folded back on such locations. The boatman is experienced and he could show us lot of colorful birds on the ride.In Cinnamon Island we could see the processing of cinnamon .We were also told the cinnamon oil is used to make mosquito repellents. Another island we visited was having an ancient Buddhist temple which was tranquil and peaceful. Apart from Statue of Buddha we can also see Hindu gods like Vishnu, Murugan etc.. in this temple.For those interested in fishing there is also a facility for the same.The boat ride which last more than an hour and a half is truly enjoyable and those visiting Bentnota should not miss it.

title: a fun ride
body: Beautiful boat safari! We did the safari twice, we liked it so much! The river has many attractions and is a fun ride. We stopped at cinammon island, buddhist temple and fish farm. Lots of birds to watch and water monitors, as well as other wild life.

The tickles of fish therapy and aroma of cinnamon would be memorable part of this rideThe entire ride comprised of some exciting underpasses (bridges) and entering through mangrove forest, crossing some small islands and an awesome flora and fauna.I would rate it to be one of the cheapest boat ride of my life.

title: Average boat ride with few attractions
body: We went with lot of expectations and the boat ride was rather bland. We managed to see monitor lizard and few other exotic birds but thats about it. Visit to Cinnamon island was informative. We also visited the Buddhist temple. The monk seemed to be fake and forced us for donations. Avoid him!

title: Captain Boat House
body: Great trip for only 2000 rupees per person...be prepared to spend another 1000 on tips throughout ride..I recall there being about 5 stops where a tip is required :)

title: Sri Lanka’s mangrove lagoons
body: Take a serene boat ride through Sri Lanka’s mangrove lagoons. Look out for the special plants and animals that live in these peaceful backwaters, from diving Little Cormorants to jumping Mud Skippers, and enjoy the beauty of these rare forests and waterways. Mangroves are essential for protecting Sri Lanka’s coast and coastal livelihoods – but they are also highly threatened. With only 0.5% of the forests remaining, Rainforest Rescue International are committed to conserving and restoring these vital habitats

title: Just a Boat Ride like any other one..Not too appealing
body: It is a tropical river with some 60 odd islands. The main activity is the boat ride on Madhu River, wherein they shall take you to some small islands .. Not too appealing , but can try it out as there is not much to do around..

title: A nice boat ride in Sri Lanka
body: Captain's Boat house is a nice experience on the whole, they first explain the route which we will be taking on a boat across the river. There are totally 64 islands in the river. The most attractive are the mangrove caves which sets the whole thing on top. The second best experience is the natural fish spa a nice 20-30mins of spa will make your feet clean. The third attraction is the cinnamon island, where these folks really show us how the cinnamon is extracted & market few of the cinnamon products. The best part was the boat driver took us to a marshy place, plucked a lotus flower near by with the stem & prepared a garland & presented it to us. The boats come with a shed & would always recommend to use one.

title: Amazing trip
body: Best part of being in Bentota is Modu River Safari. It was almost 1.5 hours journey and visited few islands there including fishing spa, cinnemon island etc. The journey was fantastic znd eorth spending of LRK 2000.
